source: RFC 0006 §5.3.2; batch R6 (B-01 of the 7.x residue audit)
statement: The authorization cookie is read as a token only when cosec.pipeline.allow-cookie-token is on, and it is off by default: a browser sends a cookie on its own, on a cross-site request too, so a host that turns it on defends against CSRF itself. With it off, a request whose only credential is that cookie is anonymous. A gateway keeps the cookie from a route whether or not it reads it (IDN-8).
guards: spring-boot:CoSecPipelineAutoConfigurationTest#the authorization cookie is a credential only with allow-cookie-token
